subject: Renewal discussion: request for rate floor, bridge credits & burst capacity
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightline.com>
Cc: Maya Rivera <maya.rivera@brightline.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: rate floor, bridge credits & burst capacity

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As you start planning Q3 campaigns, I wanted to put a couple of renewal options on the table that address the things you raised: a short-term rate floor, bridge credits for expected Q2 overages, and a burst pool for campaign weeks.

I attached a one-pager with two high-level paths (Q2_Renewal_Options.pdf). Quick summary:
- Option A: 12-month rate hold at current list with a modest committed uplift for a volume discount and a one-time bridge credit to smooth Q2 spikes.
- Option B: 6-month rate hold + flexible monthly true-up and on-demand burst pool (higher unit rate for burst).

Before I draft SOW language, can you confirm whether procurement prefers a 12-month price hold vs a 6-month flexible path? Also tagging procurement so they see the bridge-credit ask.

Next steps: if you confirm a path, I can circulate an SOW with the exact credit sizing and commit change (SOW_BridgeTerms_v2.docx).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: Q2_Renewal_Options.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightline.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Rivera <maya.rivera@brightline.com>, procurement@brightline.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: rate floor, bridge credits & burst capacity

Vanessa —

Appreciate the options. Two quick priorities from our side:
1) We need a guaranteed rate floor for at least 6 months; 12 months would be preferable if we can avoid a material premium.
2) Q2 will have a couple of campaign bursts — we want bridge credits applied to those spikes and the option to add burst capacity without a long procurement cycle.

Procurement (copied) is mainly worried about committing to a large uplift up front. If we can do a smaller committed increase + bridge credits and a defined burst pool, that might be acceptable.

Can you send a concrete proposal with numbers so we can escalate internally?

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightLine Media
samir.patel@brightline.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion: rate floor, bridge credits & burst capacity — needs numbers

Team —

Forwarding Samir's asks. BrightLine is asking for a price hold (6–12 months), bridge credits sized to cover Q2 campaign spikes, and a burst pool they can use without long lead procurement. Procurement is sensitive to big upfront commits.

Proposed internal approaches to present to customer:
- Path 1 (Conservative): 6-month rate hold at current effective rate, 120k token bridge credit, ability to purchase burst capacity at 1.35x standard rate, no commit increase required.
- Path 2 (Preferred): 12-month rate hold + 15% effective discount in exchange for a 1.2x committed usage uplift (annualized). Include a 200k token bridge credit and 30% discount on burst pool.

Questions for you:
- Ben: can we support 200k bridge credits and the listed burst pool discount for a 1.2x commit?
- Neha: any red flags on SOW language (billing triggers, definition of "burst week")?
- Lauren: pricing/finance signoff on the 15% discount vs 1.2x uplift?

Attachment: SOW_BridgeTerms_v2.docx (draft SOW with billing events). HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion: rate floor, bridge credits & burst capacity — needs numbers

Vanessa —

High-level OK on both paths; fine points below.

If we want Path 2 (preferred), here's a practical counter to present to BrightLine:
- 12-month price hold at current list, with a 12–15% blended effective discount depending on final commit.
- Commit uplift: 1.15x baseline (not 1.2x) to keep downside exposure lower for the customer.
- Bridge credit: 180k tokens to apply only to Q2 campaign windows (explicit date ranges).
- Burst pool: allow up to an additional 25% of baseline per month at a 1.25x per-token rate; any usage beyond that triggers monthly true-up at list rate.

Rationale: keeps commercial tight but gives them predictability. Finance will need final modeling, but I think this is saleable.

Neha — flagging billing-event definitions; Lauren — please run the modeled P&L and confirm margin.

Ben

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightline.com>
Cc: Maya Rivera <maya.rivera@brightline.com>, procurement@brightline.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: two final renewal paths for BrightLine (SOW attached)

Samir —

Thanks for the clarity — below are two firm options based on internal alignment. I've attached the SOW (SOW_BridgeTerms_v2.docx) and included a DocuSign link for quick execution once you confirm a path.

Option A (Conservative — no commit uplift)
- Term: 6 months rate hold at current effective rate.
- Bridge credit: 120k tokens, applied to Q2 campaign weeks (dates specified in SOW).
- Burst: on-demand at 1.35x per-token; no prepaid burst pool.
- True-up: monthly; overages billed at list after bridge credit exhaustion.

Option B (Predictable — modest commit uplift, better economics)
- Term: 12 months rate hold with blended ~13% effective discount.
- Commit: 1.15x baseline annualized (protects unit economics).
- Bridge credit: 180k tokens for Q2 campaign windows.
- Burst: additional 25% available per month at 1.25x per-token; overage true-up monthly.

Docs & next steps:
- SOW (attached) contains billing events and date ranges.
- DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123) will be sent for whichever option you pick.

If procurement prefers Option A, we can finalize the SOW quickly. If you want Option B, we need a quick email sign that the commit uplift is acceptable to finance.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW_BridgeTerms_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightline.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Rivera <maya.rivera@brightline.com>, procurement@brightline.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: two final renewal paths for BrightLine (SOW attached)

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear options and the SOW. After cycling with finance/procurement, BrightLine is inclined toward Option B (the 12-month path) but with two asks before we sign:
1) Shift bridge credit timing so at least 75% is usable in the first campaign window (we need coverage up-front).
2) Can we make the burst pool activation more self-serve (API toggle + billing flag) rather than manual approvals?

If you can update the SOW to reflect those two changes, we'll route for final exec approval and aim to e-sign by the end of the week.

Thanks,
Samir
